chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Khalid al-Qammam, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with his wife on the Day of Sacrifice before visiting the House (Kaaba). He said: 'If he had intercourse with her out of lust, he must offer a camel; and if not, a cow.' I said: 'Or a sheep?' He said: 'Or a sheep.'

And whoever performed part of the pilgrimage circuits (Tawaf) and then had intercourse with his wife, he must repeat the circuit. If he was in the Sa'i and had completed part of it, he builds upon what he has done, and upon him is the expiation. Narrated.

key_terms.السَّعْيِ: The Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim who has intercourse with their spouse during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the graduated financial expiation (kaffarah) for a pilgrim engaging in intercourse with their spouse while in Ihram, distinguishing between acts driven by lust (requiring a camel) and those that are not (requiring a cow or sheep). It further clarifies the ritual consequences, mandating the repetition of Tawaf if intercourse occurs after its completion, while allowing the pilgrim to resume Sa'i from where they left off. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the severity of breaking the sanctity of Ihram through marital relations during the Hajj rites.
